messages:
Alex W: Quick follow-up to the autoscaler RFC — I sketched an interface for the scale-controller/operator boundary. Posting notes + a couple of open questions.

Maria C: Nice, can you paste the interface signature? want to see how it models grace/drain.

Alex W: Here's the proto-ish API I'm thinking of (high level):
```go
type ScaleIntent struct {
  Pool string
  DesiredGPUs int
  Priority string // burst|reserved|background
  Reason string
  GracePeriodSeconds int // how long to wait before forced eviction
  Prewarm bool // whether to kick prewarm path on scale-out
}

// Operator endpoints
SubmitScaleIntent(intent ScaleIntent) -> intentID
QueryAdmission(pool, model) -> {allowed: bool, reason: string}
GetPoolState(pool) -> {allocated, idle, draining}
```

Shankar P: Two immediate thoughts: 1) GracePeriodSeconds needs to be bounded by pool headroom windows otherwise scale-in can stall forever. 2) We need a separate signal for "save KV cache" vs "evict immediately" — they have different costs.

Jen L: Agreed on bounded grace. Also: draining should emit a short-lived admission token so new requests can route to a warm lane instead of waiting for eviction. That avoids surprise latency spikes.

Maria C: How do we avoid long tail drains when ML jobs have large KV caches? There are models that take minutes to snapshot. We can't keep GPUs idle that long.

Alex W: Trade options I wrote down: 
- Forced eviction after grace window (fast, may increase cold starts)
- Snapshot + async restore to prewarm pool (needs ephemeral storage + bandwidth)
- Grace-aware admission: allow existing sessions to finish but divert new ones to compatible smaller model variants or other pools

Shankar P: Also consider a tiered grace: short initial grace (e.g., 15s) to finish tiny in-flight requests, then attempt a background snapshot for up to X seconds, then evict. Background snapshot should publish state to objectstore and mark workloads as restorable.

ops-bot: Notice: cluster-autoscaler applied policy patch "allow-prewarm-token" in staging. :rocket:

Jen L: About operator API surface — keep it minimal: SubmitScaleIntent and CancelIntent + QueryPool. Avoid exposing eviction details beyond reason and deadline. Operator manages drain strategy per-pool policy.

Alex W: Implementation sketch: controller computes DesiredGPUs based on metrics (queued_tokens, qps, tail_latency, reserved_commits). It calls SubmitScaleIntent with Priority derived from QoS. Operator replies with allowed+deadline. Controller waits until pool reports idle GPUs >= (current - desired) or deadline hits, then either confirm or escalate to forced reclaim.

Maria C: For metrics: we should include "prewarm_credit" in the decision — pools accumulate credits when they underutilize reserved capacity which can be spent to avoid evictions. Prevents oscillation.

Shankar P: We should also record an event stream for every intent: submitted, admitted, draining_start, snapshot_done, evicted, cancelled. Makes rollbacks + debugging easier.

Alex W: Open questions I want input on: 
1) Default grace windows: 15s / 60s / 300s? (short/medium/long)
2) Do we require operator to support snapshot+restore in phase1 or make it opt-in later?
3) Should controller expose a QueryAdmission API to upstream routing to let it choose an alternate model variant?

Maria C: My vote: default medium (60s), snapshot opt-in (phase2), expose QueryAdmission now (helps routing).

Jen L: +1 for 60s. Snapshot opt-in is fine but design the intent with a flag so we don't break future operator capabilities.

Shankar P: 60s seems reasonable as default. For long-tail we can have a per-tenant override in reserved pools. Also: hardened test harness to simulate stuck snapshot to ensure controller fallback works.

Alex W: Action items: 
- I'll implement a prototype SubmitScaleIntent + QueryAdmission (PR this week)
- Shankar to spec event stream and backoff/timeouts
- Maria to add prewarm_credit metric proposal to the autoscaler signals doc

Maria C: ack, will do.

Jen L: I'll wire the routing team to QueryAdmission so they can test JSON schema.

Alex W: cool — thanks everyone. If you have strong objections to 60s default speak now. Otherwise I'll open the prototype PR and include the API stubs. :thumbsup:
